# Mobile app and API authentication design

This assumes a first-party consumer app with moderate sensitivity; the main adjustment for banking or health data is shorter lifetimes, noted below. The core of the design is short-lived access tokens plus a rotating, device-bound refresh token tied to a server-side session record per device, which is what makes logout and lost-phone revocation work.

## Sign-in
- **Flow:** use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE through the system browser (ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS, Custom Tabs on Android), not an embedded WebView. This gives you passkeys, password managers, and social or enterprise SSO with no app changes.
- **Identity provider:** use a hosted OIDC provider unless you have a strong reason to build your own.
- **Credentials:** make passkeys the primary method, with password plus TOTP or push MFA as the fallback. Avoid SMS as the only second factor.
- **Session record:** each successful sign-in creates a `session` row holding user, device name and model, created and last-used times, a coarse IP location, the refresh-token family ID, and the device's public key.
- **Device key:** the app generates a non-exportable keypair in the Secure Enclave or StrongBox at sign-in and registers the public key with the session.

## Tokens and refresh

| Token | Format | Lifetime | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access | JWT (`sub`, `sid`, `aud`, `scope`, `exp`) | 10 min | Memory only |
| Refresh | Opaque random, stored hashed on the server | 30 days idle, 180 days absolute | Keychain / Keystore, this-device-only |

- **Rotation:** every refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old one.
- **Reuse detection:** if an already-used refresh token is presented, revoke the whole session and notify the user. Allow a grace window of about 30 seconds in which the previous token returns the same new pair, so a response lost on a flaky network does not log the user out.
- **Device binding:** the refresh request must be signed by the device key (DPoP). A refresh token copied off the device is then useless on its own.
- **Client behavior:** refresh proactively just before expiry and on a 401, with a single in-flight refresh shared by all concurrent requests. If the refresh fails with `invalid_grant`, wipe local state and return to sign-in.
- **API validation:** verify the JWT signature, `aud`, and `exp` locally. For sensitive endpoints, also check `sid` against a cached revocation set so a revoked session is cut off immediately.

## Logout
- **This device:** the app calls `POST /sessions/current/revoke`, and the server deletes the refresh family and unregisters the push token. The app then clears the Keychain entries, in-memory tokens, and cached user data, even if the network call fails.
- **Everywhere:** `POST /sessions/revoke-all` does the same for every session. Trigger it automatically on password change, credential reset, or MFA reset.
- **Residual exposure:** an already-issued access token works for up to 10 minutes on endpoints that skip the `sid` check.

## Lost phone
- **Protection before the user reacts:**
  - The refresh token sits in hardware-backed storage that is only readable while the phone is unlocked.
  - The app can optionally require biometrics or the device PIN to open.
  - Sensitive actions (changing email, payments, data export) require fresh authentication within the last 5 minutes.
- **Remote revocation:** a "Your devices" page on the web and in the app on other devices lists sessions with a revoke button for each. Revoking kills the refresh token at once and the access token within 10 minutes at most, or immediately on `sid`-checked endpoints.
- **Local data:** the app wipes its local data the next time a refresh fails.
- **Getting back in:** synced passkeys work on the replacement phone. Otherwise, use recovery codes issued at MFA enrolment or a verified-email flow with a waiting period. Any recovery revokes all existing sessions and notifies the user.
- **Alerts:** send email and push on new-device sign-in, on recovery, and on refresh-token reuse.

## Tuning for high-sensitivity apps
Use a 5-minute access token, a 7-day idle and 30-day absolute refresh lifetime, a mandatory biometric app lock, a `sid` check on every request, and app attestation (App Attest or Play Integrity) at sign-in.
